Z9PwmPQpT7.one_liner: Pairwise-judge evaluation-likeness scale identifies format cues that make conversations look like tests and increase instructed sandbagging
Z9PwmPQpT7.problem: It is unclear what leads a language model to classify a conversation as an evaluation, whether format plays a part, and whether changing the format changes behavior.
Z9PwmPQpT7.method: Judge models from eight families pick the more evaluation-like conversation in pairs, a pairwise preference model turns the choices into one evaluation-likeness scale, and hand-defined format cues are ranked by how far they move the score. Hazardous-knowledge questions are then rewritten one format step at a time, and models are told in the system prompt to underperform if they believe they are being evaluated.
Z9PwmPQpT7.key_idea: Rank hand-defined format cues by their effect on a pairwise-preference evaluation-likeness score, then test them causally by rewriting the same question's format step by step.
Z9PwmPQpT7.evidence: Judges from eight families across 33 conversation pools and over 158,000 trials (per a reviewer), stepwise rewrites of hazardous-knowledge questions, and an instructed-sandbagging test.
Z9PwmPQpT7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and well organized, with a useful evaluation-likeness metric and a large, broad setup covering many judges and benchmarks.
Z9PwmPQpT7.main_concern: Construct validity is weak: the rewrites are not single-feature interventions, the study tests format recognition rather than evaluation awareness, and benchmark familiarity is an acknowledged confounder.

dL4GcShP3x.one_liner: Trains code-localization agents by contracting an explicit candidate set monotonically, crediting each exclusion with volume and coverage-ceiling potentials.
dL4GcShP3x.problem: Free-form localization answers give no training signal for correctly excluding plausible but off-path code, because discarded locations never appear in the answer.
dL4GcShP3x.method: C3L binds the prediction to an explicit survivor set that the agent contracts monotonically from read-only evidence; a logarithmic weighted-volume potential rewards effective contraction and a reachable localization ceiling charges coverage loss when a necessary location is discarded. Turns are compared across rollouts by survivor-set signature, and an execution-verified label cache credits valid repairs outside the reference patch.
dL4GcShP3x.key_idea: Make each exclusion an irreversible state transition on a survivor set and price it with a log-volume potential and a coverage-ceiling potential for turn-level credit.
dL4GcShP3x.evidence: SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro (Python) and LocBench with a 4B backbone against retrained same-size baselines and a frozen 30B-A3B agent, plus downstream repair with a fixed backend.
dL4GcShP3x.claimed_gains: With a 4B backbone, exceeds the strongest retrained same-size baseline by 6.2-7.2 mean-F1 points on SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro (Python) and LocBench, and raises a fixed repair backend's one-shot resolve rate from 37.33% to 40.40%.
dL4GcShP3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that turning exclusions into observable, creditable events is a clear and compelling formulation, with controlled experiments (matched baselines, confidence intervals) and thorough attribution studies.
dL4GcShP3x.main_concern: Irreversible pruning over a fixed candidate universe limits recovery from retrieval misses (initial reference coverage is only 58.3% on Pro-Python), and evaluation covers only Python repositories and two related backbones.

8rMHzpEIJM.one_liner: NexusFL fits a tree surrogate of coalition utility each round to select interacting client subsets in federated learning.
8rMHzpEIJM.problem: Client selection in federated learning is combinatorial, and individual-importance or pairwise methods cannot capture higher-order, evolving redundancy and complementarity among clients.
8rMHzpEIJM.method: A tree-based surrogate of coalition utility, refit each round, captures client interactions up to a controllable order and both proposes the candidate pool and chooses the aggregation set; its additive decomposition scores each candidate by its own effect plus its interactions with clients already selected.
8rMHzpEIJM.key_idea: Learn a per-round tree surrogate of subset utility whose additive interaction decomposition scores candidate clients given those already selected.
8rMHzpEIJM.evidence: Twelve settings on nine datasets against Shapley-based and other selectors, with ablations, a selection-regret analysis and a convergence analysis under stated assumptions.
8rMHzpEIJM.claimed_gains: Attains the highest trajectory-mean accuracy in every setting, by up to 12 points over the strongest baseline.
8rMHzpEIJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear, the design (recency-weighted reservoir, candidate pool, tree surrogate) well adapted to federated learning, and the theory and nine-dataset evaluation convincing.
8rMHzpEIJM.main_concern: Coalition utility evaluation is costly (46% of per-round time for CNN/CIFAR-10 and 85% for DistilBERT/FinGPT), and reviewers also question FedAvg getting half the compute and whether higher-order gains are confounded with tree depth.

E3zB17tCkW.one_liner: Groups rubric diagnoses into independent defect events and learns their costs from preferences to build rewards for open-ended post-training.
E3zB17tCkW.problem: In open-ended post-training, judge scores concentrate in a narrow range that may not rank close responses reliably, and aggregating rubric diagnoses double-counts one defect across criteria, collapses independent defects, or miscalibrates penalties.
E3zB17tCkW.method: CARMA groups evidence-linked diagnoses that one semantic repair can resolve into a single event and learns defect costs from same-prompt preferences. It adjusts an independently obtained holistic score with event-level penalties.
E3zB17tCkW.key_idea: Count independent defects by whether one semantic repair fixes them, then penalize each event by a cost learned from same-prompt preferences.
E3zB17tCkW.evidence: Two model scales on Chinese and English writing tasks with automatic and human preference evaluations, plus ablation and corruption experiments, using Qwen-family models (from reviews).
E3zB17tCkW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that counting repairs rather than violated criteria is a useful way to handle double-counted and collapsed defects, with clear improvements over baselines across two scales and two languages.
E3zB17tCkW.main_concern: Reliability depends on LLM judgment: event grouping gets 190 of 218 pair decisions right, the same judge model builds rewards and evaluates, and results cover only Qwen models.

bCjfnDnvJI.one_liner: Connects independently trained states at matched loss levels with fitted nonlinear paths and analyzes per-example residuals along them.
bCjfnDnvJI.problem: Loss-landscape and mode-connectivity studies focus on converged solutions, leaving open how the geometry is organized while the model is still learning from the training data.
bCjfnDnvJI.method: They study connectivity between independently trained states at matched objective levels (loss-level connectivity), fit nonlinear paths that approximately preserve the endpoint-defined loss, and analyze example-wise residuals along those paths.
bCjfnDnvJI.key_idea: Compare independently trained states at matched loss values, connect them with fitted nonlinear paths of near-constant loss, and read data-dependent structure from per-example residuals along the path.
bCjfnDnvJI.evidence: In the settings examined, matched-loss states are connected by fitted nonlinear paths across multiple training stages; reviews also cite corruption-ratio and label-corruption experiments and cross-optimizer connectivity.
bCjfnDnvJI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the loss-level connectivity notion conceptually interesting and the sample-level finding (separation of corrupted examples beyond endpoint losses) informative.
bCjfnDnvJI.main_concern: It is unclear what loss-level connectivity reveals beyond standard mode connectivity, and the contribution is not distinguished from prior per-example and mode-connectivity work such as Lottery Tickets on a Data Diet.

gOepJXypgI.one_liner: Separates example order, exposure, and recent-data support to show curriculum-induced grokking delays come from restricted support.
gOepJXypgI.problem: Curricula can delay grokking by orders of magnitude, but a curriculum changes example order, exposure, and support at once, so the cause is unclear.
gOepJXypgI.method: They define order, exposure, and support as functions of the training step and vary each separately on six algorithmic tasks using global sorting, within-epoch sorting, held random or difficulty-selected subsets, and replay of examples.
gOepJXypgI.key_idea: Delay tracks how long training is confined to an unrepresentative difficulty slice (transient support), not total exposure or fine-grained order; replaying examples from the whole set restores the transition.
gOepJXypgI.evidence: Controlled experiments on six algorithmic tasks (including modular addition and GCD) with exposure fixed, sorted-stretch length sweeps, subset dwell-time controls, and replay fractions; reviews note training logs are released.
gOepJXypgI.claimed_gains: With exposure fixed, global sorting prevents the transition within the step budget on most tasks, within-epoch sorting costs at most 1.9x with the main difficulty keys, and the delay on modular addition sets in at sorted stretches of about 22 steps.
gOepJXypgI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the experimental separation of total exposure from its temporal arrangement, the large consistent effects across tasks, and the clearly stated research question.
gOepJXypgI.main_concern: The key variables (order, exposure, support, confinement duration) lack precise formal definitions, and the evidence covers six tasks with one difficulty metric each and a prefix-matched control on only two.

fuPa6FiW3P.one_liner: Local search yields a 4-approximation for fair diversity maximization with constant group count and a 2-approximation for two groups.
fuPa6FiW3P.problem: The best known guarantee for selecting exactly k_i points per group while maximizing the minimum pairwise distance is m+1, which grows linearly with the number of groups m.
fuPa6FiW3P.method: A local-search framework keeps all group quotas exact while progressively eliminating violations of the diversity objective, using repairs that swap a constant number of points across groups; a specialized algorithm handles two groups.
fuPa6FiW3P.key_idea: Repair distance violations by swapping a bounded number of points across groups while preserving quotas, with existence of such repairs proved via non-overlapping balls and the Steinitz lemma.
fuPa6FiW3P.evidence: Theoretical proofs of the approximation ratios (4 for any constant number of groups, 2 for two groups), with the abstract stating the factor 2 is optimal unless P=NP; reviews note there are no experiments.
fuPa6FiW3P.claimed_gains: A 4-approximation for any constant number of groups versus the previous m+1, and a 2-approximation for two groups versus the previous factor of 3.
fuPa6FiW3P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is a theoretical advance in approximation guarantees, obtained through a non-trivial local-search and repair technique.
fuPa6FiW3P.main_concern: The search over repairs of size up to (2m+1)^m-1 makes the running time very large and unstated in the theorem, so the gain over m+1 is narrow, and Definition 6 has an index inconsistency in the main proof.

YheEB8Vu7b.one_liner: Instruction-tunes Llama-3.1-8B on property-annotated Swiss-Prot proteins, then applies natural-sequence-anchored DPO to improve domain recovery.
YheEB8Vu7b.problem: Protein language models can generate plausible sequences, but reliable control over multiple user-specified properties remains limited.
YheEB8Vu7b.method: Aria tunes Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 350k Swiss-Prot proteins described by a random subset of thirteen property descriptors in the prompt, then runs family-targeted DPO rounds with natural sequences as preferred responses to improve structural confidence and domain recovery.
YheEB8Vu7b.key_idea: Condition generation on property descriptors written in the prompt, then run DPO with natural family sequences as preferred responses plus an NLL term on them.
YheEB8Vu7b.evidence: Cluster-separated evaluation proteins, property functions recomputed on outputs, prompt-mismatch controls, ESMFold pLDDT, and Pfam domain recovery across PF00416 and three additional families, averaged over two training seeds.
YheEB8Vu7b.claimed_gains: One DPO stage raises mean ESMFold pLDDT by 8.2 points in PF00416, and across three additional families requested-domain recovery rises by 28.7-43.6 percentage points after three rounds.
YheEB8Vu7b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recomputing the directly measurable descriptors and the prompt-mismatch controls give a credible test of whether the model follows the requested specification.
YheEB8Vu7b.main_concern: The DPO gains may come from further fitting natural family sequences rather than from structure-based preference, since no matched continued-SFT or NLL-only control on the same sequences is reported.

Zsvg0RqVl5.one_liner: Locates a quality axis in reasoning-text embeddings and builds it into contrastive learning with symmetric RoPE and ordinal loss.
Zsvg0RqVl5.problem: Text embeddings of RL-generated quality reasoning entangle perceptual quality with scene content and wording, so it is unclear what transferable quality information they carry.
Zsvg0RqVl5.method: QAxis finds a quality axis from MOS-conditioned variation in reasoning text, then trains a 0.3B image encoder contrastively with a symmetric RoPE that makes cross-modal similarity depend on semantic match and agreement along quality coordinates, plus axis-wise ordinal learning.
Zsvg0RqVl5.key_idea: Extract a MOS-conditioned quality direction from reasoning embeddings; a rotation ties similarity to quality coordinates and an ordinal loss ranks images along that axis.
Zsvg0RqVl5.evidence: Analyses of contrastive training dynamics and controlled domain shifts, evaluation on seven IQA benchmarks, and component ablations of description consensus, rotation, and ranking.
Zsvg0RqVl5.claimed_gains: With a 0.3B image encoder, direct axis projection reaches average PLCC/SRCC of 0.811/0.796 across seven benchmarks, rising to 0.816/0.800 with the complete image representation.
Zsvg0RqVl5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the search for a shared quality direction interesting and the inference simple (a single projection onto a fixed direction) yet competitive across the seven-dataset average.
Zsvg0RqVl5.main_concern: The evidence does not show the quality axis itself drives the gains, since the axis is found from MOS labels and the gains may come from the added ranking loss, scoring head, or trainable encoder.

YhGiD7wpkt.one_liner: Matched page edits show SFT shifts search-agent stopping decisions from answer-like strings toward entity mentions.
YhGiD7wpkt.problem: It is unclear which features of a retrieved page drive a search agent's decision to answer or keep searching, and how fine-tuning changes them.
YhGiD7wpkt.method: They switch an entity mention, an answer-like string, and the supporting fact on or off with matched page edits, test instruction-tuned models from three families plus SFT-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and check real search episodes.
YhGiD7wpkt.key_idea: Matched edits that independently toggle the entity mention, the answer-like string, and the supporting fact isolate which cue the stopping decision responds to.
YhGiD7wpkt.evidence: Controlled page edits on instruction-tuned models from three families, SFT on single answer-or-search decisions, preregistered held-out pages, and real search episodes.
YhGiD7wpkt.claimed_gains: After SFT, the effect of an entity mention on stopping rises from 6 to 47 percentage points and that of an answer-like string falls from 29 to 5, and the fine-tuned agent says the fact is missing for 96% of mention-only pages but answers on 54%.
YhGiD7wpkt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important for search agents and the study is well organized, combining controlled comparisons, real search episodes, and held-out checks that separate preregistered from exploratory tests.
YhGiD7wpkt.main_concern: The main finding rests on a constructed SFT set where the entity's page almost perfectly predicts the stopping label (AUROC 0.98), so it is unclear how often the behavior arises in agents trained on other data.

LYRkZDWYpO.one_liner: A learned decision-tree policy decides per query when to stop graph-based nearest-neighbor search, reallocating visits across queries.
LYRkZDWYpO.problem: Finding one more true neighbor can take far more graph visits for one query than for another, yet each hit counts equally toward average recall at a fixed k.
LYRkZDWYpO.method: TraCANN records search time and recovered neighbors at successive stopping points per query during training, then dynamic programming assigns a frontier width and total visit budget to each leaf of a decision tree under a shared recall target; queries reaching 32 visits consult the tree once and either return or continue.
LYRkZDWYpO.key_idea: Allocate search visits unevenly across queries with a dynamic-programming-built decision tree on early search progress, so easy queries stop early and hard ones continue.
LYRkZDWYpO.evidence: Four public ANN benchmarks at three recall targets on one and eight CPU cores, plus analysis of when reallocating visits reduces total cost and a bound on the cost gap between discrete and fractional action assignments.
LYRkZDWYpO.claimed_gains: Higher throughput than the fastest qualifying baseline at each of three recall targets on both one and eight CPU cores across four benchmarks; no figures are given in the abstract.
LYRkZDWYpO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the speedups large and consistent across datasets and the formulation of early termination as resource allocation across queries simple and interesting.
LYRkZDWYpO.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the speedup comes from the query-adaptive policy rather than implementation details such as AVX-512 VNNI dot products, since no fixed-width, non-learned ablation on the same code is reported.

jA6DsjW60P.one_liner: Trains latent world models to predict the latent difference between two actions' futures, branched from one simulator state.
jA6DsjW60P.problem: Latent world models are trained to predict what happens next, so nothing in their objective separates what an action caused from what merely co-occurred with it.
jA6DsjW60P.method: From one saved simulator state they run the dynamics under an action and a reference action and train the model to predict the latent difference, using an effect loss, a support loss (where the action enters), a propagation loss (where its effect travels), and invariance losses.
jA6DsjW60P.key_idea: Supervise the difference between latent futures under an action and a reference action from the same state, with separate losses for effect, support, propagation, and invariance.
jA6DsjW60P.evidence: A synthetic object-aligned system, pixel-based LeWM experiments with a control trained on the same data, natural-action Push-T tests, and three independently generated CausalWorld benchmarks.
jA6DsjW60P.claimed_gains: Support supervision finds the directly intervened object in 99.95% of test cases and propagation recovery reaches edge AUROC 0.975 vs 0.624; the effect loss lowers latent effect error by 28.4% (3/3 seeds), physical effect error by 13.5%, and responsive effect error by about 20% on CausalWorld under physics shifts.
jA6DsjW60P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is meaningful, the same-data control separates the objective's benefit from extra data, and negative results are reported openly.
jA6DsjW60P.main_concern: The gains do not establish a useful capability beyond effect prediction: planning does not improve (and can degrade), and full Do-JEPA sometimes underperforms the simpler paired-data control.

QlPS71AW8a.one_liner: Compares Base, SFT, and Aligned checkpoints of seven model lineages in repeated social dilemmas to measure the memory curse.
QlPS71AW8a.problem: It is unknown how post-training changes cooperation in repeated play, in particular whether it affects the memory curse, where cooperation falls when agents see more past rounds.
QlPS71AW8a.method: Copies of each checkpoint play one another for 200 rounds across seven social dilemmas with visible history limited to the last two or forty rounds, comparing pretrained, SFT, and preference- or reward-optimized checkpoints within each lineage.
QlPS71AW8a.key_idea: Hold the model lineage fixed and vary the post-training stage and visible-history length in self-play to isolate post-training's effect on the memory curse.
QlPS71AW8a.evidence: 21 checkpoints across seven lineages and seven social dilemmas, with 200-round self-play, payoff-parameter sweeps, and comparisons of one-shot versus repeated play and final-round versus future-interaction instructions.
QlPS71AW8a.claimed_gains: No gains claimed; post-training amplifies the decline, with history-induced declines at each post-trained stage exceeding Base's in six of seven lineages.
QlPS71AW8a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conclusion that post-training reduces cooperation is counterintuitive and the coverage of models, checkpoints, and games is extensive.
QlPS71AW8a.main_concern: The paper does not identify the mechanism by which post-training amplifies the memory curse, and its proposed explanation conflicts with the results in Table 25.

MRRGGGGiux.one_liner: Introduces metric robustness to bound downstream classifier generalization by the generalization of the learned metric.
MRRGGGGiux.problem: Metric learning theory studies the learned metric's quality but not how the metric affects downstream classification, and whether over-parameterization causes overfitting in metric learning is open.
MRRGGGGiux.method: They define metric robustness of classification algorithms with respect to metrics and derive classification generalization guarantees through it for several metrics and classifiers. They also prove that over-parameterization does not necessarily cause overfitting for a class of distance metric learning methods.
MRRGGGGiux.key_idea: Define metric robustness, the sensitivity of a classifier's loss to the metric, and bound the classification generalization gap by the metric's generalization gap.
MRRGGGGiux.evidence: Theoretical proofs, including a proposition that metric losses can vanish while the classification generalization gap is maximal; experiments reported by reviewers use a single dataset.
MRRGGGGiux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified framework linking metric generalization to downstream classification generalization is well motivated, with detailed proofs and a treatment of over-parameterization.
MRRGGGGiux.main_concern: The novelty over existing algorithmic-robustness analyses is unclear, the assumptions (e.g. a label-pure partition fixed in advance) are hard to apply in practice, and experiments use only one dataset.

NjWEJGu9tW.one_liner: An atlas of Big Five personality representations tests whether portraits, steering, or both match 420 real people's facet profiles.
NjWEJGu9tW.problem: LM personality work treats the Big Five domains as five independent coarse dials judged by trait-sounding output, without testing whether a model can match an individual's facet-level questionnaire profile.
NjWEJGu9tW.method: Across five open-weight models and 420 people, they score per-person agreement with Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, compare written portraits, activation steering, and both, and analyze facet directions from three tasks and how steering one facet moves others.
NjWEJGu9tW.key_idea: Score person-level fidelity with concordance correlation, which penalizes exaggeration, and compare facet steering directions across tasks to show traits behave like correlated profiles, not independent dials.
NjWEJGu9tW.evidence: Five open-weight models, 420 people, three LLM readers recovering facets from generated text, a small human validation at the Big Five level, and behavioral experiments.
NjWEJGu9tW.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (cut off); it reports that OLMo 3 starts picking up facet covariance by about 0.2% of pretraining steps.
NjWEJGu9tW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is thorough, uses concordance rather than plain correlation, covers facets across several models and 420 people, and reports negative and mixed results candidly.
NjWEJGu9tW.main_concern: Facet-level fidelity is judged mainly by LLM readers with small, domain-level human validation, which risks circularity and leaves behavioral fidelity and the added value of steering over portraits unproven.

WXjd30H2gJ.one_liner: Shows text-only classifiers and untrained networks pass probe tests on EvalAwareBench, undermining content-matched evidence for evaluation awareness.
WXjd30H2gJ.problem: Linear probes are read as evidence that models represent being evaluated, on the assumption that content-matched designs make a separating probe detect recognition of the cue rather than the cue's wording.
WXjd30H2gJ.method: A pre-registered protocol on 17 open models runs bag-of-words classifiers and 17 untrained networks (0.5B to 7B parameters) through the standard per-cue probe test on the eight cues of EvalAwareBench, then adds a lexically matched test that replaces answer-format instructions with new ones sharing no words.
WXjd30H2gJ.key_idea: Apply bag-of-words and untrained-network baselines to the probe test, then use lexically matched replacement cues to find what survives both.
WXjd30H2gJ.evidence: Pre-registered tests on 17 open models and eight EvalAwareBench cues, including a mixed-source evaluation and deployment set and a full-factorial run.
WXjd30H2gJ.claimed_gains: A bag-of-words classifier separates all eight cues (median AUROC 0.89-1.00) and 17 untrained networks pass the probe test on every cue; activations add a small but robust increment beyond the words.
WXjd30H2gJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is transparent and rigorous, with pre-registration, reported failed predictions, and a useful lexical audit that challenges how probe success is interpreted.
WXjd30H2gJ.main_concern: Narrow scope and contribution: conclusions rest on one benchmark, one token position and linear readouts, and the central warning about probes exploiting wording is seen as already established.

7zBAQRpZcZ.one_liner: Allocating rank across mean and residual per-sample gradient modes initializes LoRA branches and supervises a prompt-conditioned signed-weight router.
7zBAQRpZcZ.problem: Standard and aggregate-gradient LoRA methods apply one shared low-rank update to every input, suppressing systematic per-sample differences in preferred update directions.
7zBAQRpZcZ.method: SGB-LoRA decomposes per-sample calibration gradients into a shared mean and centered residuals, allocates a fixed per-matrix rank budget across mean and residual modes by gradient energy and compressibility, and initializes LoRA branches from the retained bases. Refitted per-sample coordinates supervise a lightweight prompt-side router predicting signed branch weights before joint router-branch optimization.
7zBAQRpZcZ.key_idea: Decompose per-sample calibration gradients into mean and spectral residual modes to allocate rank, initialize LoRA branches, and supervise a prompt-side router predicting signed branch weights.
7zBAQRpZcZ.evidence: Supported by an optimality proof for calibration-gradient reconstruction within a fixed spectral family and experiments on instruction following, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and commonsense reasoning.
7zBAQRpZcZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting per-sample gradient variation beyond the mean gradient to jointly initialize adapters and supervise conditional routing under a fixed rank budget is well motivated.
7zBAQRpZcZ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing direct comparisons with conditional LoRA mixtures and per-sample gradient-routing baselines (such as MoLE, HydraLoRA, MixLoRA, ELREA, and GradientSpace) and note that theory covers only gradient reconstruction.

ODSOEKvyoC.one_liner: Monosemantic Retrieval learns weights over sparse-autoencoder features and scores documents through features shared with the query.
ODSOEKvyoC.problem: Dense embedding superposition and high-dimensional cosine similarity can dilute features that determine query-specific relevance.
ODSOEKvyoC.method: Monosemantic Retrieval learns per-feature retrieval weights over sparse-autoencoder representations and indexes documents in these coordinates. Scoring uses sparse query-document feature overlap, with interpretable features supporting retrieval control.
ODSOEKvyoC.key_idea: Replace dense cosine scoring with learned weighting of the sparse monosemantic features shared by a query and document.
ODSOEKvyoC.evidence: Evaluation spans 66 benchmarks across eleven domains, with reviews describing nine SAE backbones, retrieval-index comparisons, and component ablations.
ODSOEKvyoC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate interpretable feature-based retrieval and the broad evaluation with component ablations.
ODSOEKvyoC.main_concern: The quality-cost claims omit encoding costs and lack consistent storage accounting and end-to-end latency measurements.

4Tj5BruQjF.one_liner: ReNIO converts student-teacher token-probability ratios into trajectory weights that emphasize likely incorrect reasoning prefixes.
4Tj5BruQjF.problem: Uniform on-policy distillation ignores differences in how informative correct and incorrect student trajectories are.
4Tj5BruQjF.method: ReNIO identifies influential tokens using student-to-teacher probability ratios and aggregates them into normalized sample weights. The weights emphasize likely negative trajectories without final-answer correctness labels, retaining compatibility with truncated rollouts.
4Tj5BruQjF.key_idea: Aggregate prefix-conditioned student-teacher probability ratios into sample weights that favor likely negative reasoning trajectories.
4Tj5BruQjF.evidence: Correct-only and incorrect-only filtering experiments and mathematical-reasoning and code-generation evaluations cover both OPD and on-policy self-distillation.
4Tj5BruQjF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value upweighting informative negative trajectories using already available probabilities without requiring completed answers.
4Tj5BruQjF.main_concern: The cost-accuracy advantage over simpler negative-rollout filtering is not fully quantified, and small gains lack training-run uncertainty.

85Z2N9E3ZL.one_liner: Tensor-train contractions mix channels across graded CDE levels while diagonal decay preserves efficient scans and additive decomposition.
85Z2N9E3ZL.problem: Diagonal sequence transitions restrict cross-channel interactions, whereas dense transitions are expensive to compose.
85Z2N9E3ZL.method: TD-CDE uses diagonal input-dependent decay at each level and tensor-train contractions of previous-level states with gated path increments. Multilinearity yields exact single-layer decompositions, while within-step Chen terms improve discretization under subsampling.
85Z2N9E3ZL.key_idea: Separate diagonal temporal evolution from tensor-train channel mixing between interaction levels, enabling additive decompositions under fixed gates.
85Z2N9E3ZL.evidence: Representation analysis, interaction profiling, resolution-transfer tests, and the Log-NCDE benchmark evaluate the tensorized model.
85Z2N9E3ZL.claimed_gains: Within-step Chen terms yield 6 versus 30 flipped predictions out of 1,275 on SelfRegulationSCP1, and TD-CDE has the fourth-best average rank of eleven models.
85Z2N9E3ZL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mathematical treatment of higher-order temporal interactions and the analysis of discretization.
85Z2N9E3ZL.main_concern: Expressivity and exact-decomposition claims require clearer scope, especially when input-dependent gates affect their interpretation.

H8sL39AUYe.one_liner: Amortizes conditional diffusion recourse over a conjugate cost-curve prior using target-first inverted training-pair sampling.
H8sL39AUYe.problem: Generative algorithmic recourse models typically bake in a single fixed cost function during training, while inference-time guidance toward individual user cost preferences is slow and degrades under cost mismatch.
H8sL39AUYe.method: ACCORD trains a conditional diffusion model over user cost functions drawn from a conjugate prior formed by linear combinations of random cost curves capturing weighted, asymmetric, and range-dependent preferences. Using unpaired positive and negative instances, it exploits conjugacy to invert pair construction—sampling positive target instances first and drawing compatible posterior costs—without searching over positives per cost.
H8sL39AUYe.key_idea: Condition a recourse diffusion model on user cost functions drawn from a conjugate linear cost-curve prior while inverting pair sampling to draw positive targets before posterior costs.
H8sL39AUYe.evidence: Theoretical risk analysis of inverted versus forward sampling and experiments on synthetic and real-world tabular datasets (including COMPAS and HELOC per reviews) against search-based and generative recourse baselines.
H8sL39AUYe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing a single generative recourse model across heterogeneous user cost preferences via a conjugate prior and inverted pair sampling is well integrated and practically motivated.
H8sL39AUYe.main_concern: Theoretical guarantees assume full-dataset sampling and shared optima that conflict with top-v candidate truncation in Algorithm 1, while evaluations draw data-compatible test preferences and do not consistently beat baselines like FACE.

G3RAbYdT06.one_liner: Builds an aerial post-hurricane 3D point-cloud benchmark pairing building/scene segmentation with spatially grounded VQA and referring segmentation.
G3RAbYdT06.problem: Existing post-disaster multimodal benchmarks rely primarily on 2D imagery, limiting evaluation of 3D geometric damage cues such as roof collapse, debris extent, occlusion, and spatial building relationships.
G3RAbYdT06.method: 3D-VL-Fly constructs UAV-derived 3D point-cloud scenes from post-Hurricane Ian (2022) aerial imagery annotated with building instance segmentation, road and tree semantic segmentation, and independent per-building damage attributes. It pairs these scenes with spatially grounded VQA across eight question families alongside 3D referring and reasoning segmentation tasks.
G3RAbYdT06.key_idea: Reconstruct post-disaster UAV imagery into annotated 3D point clouds with per-building attributes to jointly evaluate 3D visual question answering and language-referred segmentation.
G3RAbYdT06.evidence: Evaluates native 3D point-cloud models and multi-view rendered 2D MLLMs alongside majority/constant baselines on held-out geographic scenes from Hurricane Ian.
G3RAbYdT06.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate extending 3D vision-language VQA and segmentation to real UAV post-disaster scenes and commend the inclusion of held-out area splits and majority-class baselines.
G3RAbYdT06.main_concern: The dataset covers a small number of buildings from a single hurricane event where ground-truth labels use high-resolution 2D photos unseen by 3D models, and constant or majority-class baselines beat evaluated models on VQA and damage attributes.

YpfP25KOnB.one_liner: Uses position-dependent corruption to test how supervision allocation shapes in-context learning in diffusion language models.
YpfP25KOnB.problem: It is unclear why next-token pretraining produces in-context learners more effectively than masked and diffusion objectives with distributed supervision.
YpfP25KOnB.method: The authors connect autoregressive training to Bayes-optimal episodic prediction, quantify uncertainty reduction from observing the future, and compare matched AR, MLM, and diffusion transformers. A position-dependent corruption process allocates more training to earlier context and later targets.
YpfP25KOnB.key_idea: Bias masking positions so training more often supplies earlier observations and later prediction targets, directly testing sequential supervision allocation.
YpfP25KOnB.evidence: Matched models are evaluated on diverse algorithmic few-shot tasks under iterative generation and multiple diffusion objectives, with continued pretransfer to LLaDA-8B.
YpfP25KOnB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-objective question is interesting and that matched interventions and LLaDA-8B continued pretraining provide useful controlled evidence.
YpfP25KOnB.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical interpretation stronger than the entropy result and question novelty and experimental isolation relative to prior position-dependent masking.

8NNPhweH0D.one_liner: Learns O(2)-equivariant self-supervised cell representations directly from individual mRNA molecule coordinates via hierarchical geometric moments.
8NNPhweH0D.problem: Standard spatial transcriptomics representations collapse cells into gene-count vectors, discarding intracellular spatial organization of individual mRNA molecules.
8NNPhweH0D.method: Molm models each cell as a molecular point cloud, hierarchically grouping molecules into learned localization programs and computing exact rotation- and reflection-equivariant geometric moments at each layer, trained self-supervised by agreeing across random subsampled detection views.
8NNPhweH0D.key_idea: Computes exact O(2)-equivariant moments of learned molecular localization measures across hierarchical layers and trains via self-supervised agreement between subsampled molecule clouds.
8NNPhweH0D.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic subcellular benchmark (resampled from real cells) and real spatial transcriptomics datasets (Lung, DCIS) for cell-type and morphology prediction.
8NNPhweH0D.claimed_gains: Recovers an arrangement-only cell subtype at 0.864 balanced accuracy within each cell type (chance 1/3).
8NNPhweH0D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate moving beyond gene-count vectors to molecule-level subcellular modeling with an O(2)-equivariant geometric moment architecture and subsampling self-supervision.
8NNPhweH0D.main_concern: Reviewers note that evidence of discovering biologically meaningful subcellular organization comes from synthetic benchmarks, while real-data gains over count baselines on cell typing are small.

sD8lLwdh7N.one_liner: Trains agents end-to-end with GRPO to invoke summarization and subagent-delegation meta-tools beyond a single context window.
sD8lLwdh7N.problem: Agents that accumulate full interaction histories exceed fixed context windows, preventing end-to-end RL training on long-horizon tasks.
sD8lLwdh7N.method: CARP encapsulates history compaction and subagent delegation as meta-tools and records each generated token's local conditioning context in a token tree, enabling exact log-probability gradient updates with GRPO without fitting the whole rollout into one window.
sD8lLwdh7N.key_idea: Stores per-token conditioning contexts in token trees so RL can train compaction and delegation meta-tools across arbitrarily long horizons.
sD8lLwdh7N.evidence: Evaluated with GRPO on synthetic counting tasks exceeding the context window and OOLONG transfer tasks.
sD8lLwdh7N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the token-tree training formulation clean and broadly applicable for bounding peak memory during long-horizon RL.
sD8lLwdh7N.main_concern: Novelty over prior RL context-management and delegation methods (e.g., MemAgent, ReSum, Context-Folding) is limited, baselines are missing, and experiments use only one or two seeds.

j9nzDz0bKh.one_liner: Splitting liquid-network states into adaptive and persistent subspaces separates rapid writing from long-term information retention.
j9nzDz0bKh.problem: LTC hidden-state decay couples new-information writing with old-information loss because fast updates and long retention require opposing dynamics.
j9nzDz0bKh.method: SSD-LTC decomposes hidden state into an adaptive liquid component and a persistent component with an input-dependent write rate. The paper analyzes attenuation, the writing-retention tradeoff, boundedness, and stability.
j9nzDz0bKh.key_idea: An input-dependent write rate controls preservation in a dedicated persistent subspace while the liquid subspace retains adaptive LTC dynamics.
j9nzDz0bKh.evidence: Experiments cover ten regularly sampled and eight irregularly sampled benchmarks, with delayed-recall and component-exchange tests examining the memory mechanism.
j9nzDz0bKh.claimed_gains: SSD-LTC improves classification accuracy by 2.2 to 8.0 percentage points and reduces regression and forecasting errors by up to 30% compared with the stated baselines.
j9nzDz0bKh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the decomposition directly addresses the writing-retention tradeoff and that delayed-recall and component-exchange tests support the mechanism.
j9nzDz0bKh.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that gains may come from generic gated memory rather than the proposed decomposition and criticize the missing ODE-LSTM comparison.

xmP3m8VBOk.one_liner: Reuses stale prior gradients via error-bounded Gaussian proposals and randomized corrections to accelerate exact posterior sampling.
xmP3m8VBOk.problem: Posterior sampling with learned priors repeatedly evaluates costly gradients at nearby states, wasting computation without exact law-preserving reuse.
xmP3m8VBOk.method: Posterior Entrances (PE) combines a retained gradient with a computable current-error bound to build a Gaussian proposal and cheap screening test, followed by randomized current-gradient queries that preserve the exact conditional distribution. The authors also examine information-bearing diffusion states via a four-branch 32-step continuation procedure (E32).
xmP3m8VBOk.key_idea: Turns a cached gradient and its computable error bound into a screened Gaussian proposal plus randomized current-gradient correction that provably preserves the exact finite-horizon conditional sampling law.
xmP3m8VBOk.evidence: Proves exact law preservation and net-query conditions, evaluated on four trained 64D optical-digit prior configurations, a 30-image study, and 100 degraded ImageNet validation photos for E32.
xmP3m8VBOk.claimed_gains: Across four trained-model configurations, fresh-FORS/PE ratios are 1.354–1.369 for gradient queries and 1.135–1.296 for pipeline time; a 30-image evaluation yields 28.60% fewer queries and 7.18% lower time.
xmP3m8VBOk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that certificate-based gradient reuse preserving the exact conditional transition law with careful query/time accounting is a clean, technically sound contribution.
xmP3m8VBOk.main_concern: Reviewers point out that exact PE requires restrictive global curvature bounds tested only on toy 64D log-cosh optical-digit priors, while the real-image E32 experiment is an unrelated, approximate diffusion procedure.

s2rrW2v1sO.one_liner: Analyzes training-path resistance in consistency tuning and adds uniform noise-level sampling to Easy Consistency Tuning for one-step generation.
s2rrW2v1sO.problem: Low average consistency loss does not guarantee strong one-step image generation because uneven noise-level sampling leaves bottlenecks along the training path.
s2rrW2v1sO.method: The authors analyze a chain model of consistency tuning to derive a pre-training path-resistance metric based on least-trained neighboring noise pairs below the generation start level, and propose Uniform Consistency Tuning (UCT), which modifies ECT's noise-level distribution with uniform draws.
s2rrW2v1sO.key_idea: Derive training-path resistance from least-trained neighboring noise levels and mix uniform noise-level sampling into Easy Consistency Tuning to remove high-noise bottlenecks.
s2rrW2v1sO.evidence: Chain-model theoretical analysis and small-budget one-step generation experiments on CIFAR-10 (six paired seeds) and ImageNet-64.
s2rrW2v1sO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity of the one-line UCT modification and its consistent paired-seed one-step FID improvements on CIFAR-10 at small budgets.
s2rrW2v1sO.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the independent-level chain model ignores neural parameter sharing, theoretical results largely restate prior telescoping bounds, and the ECT lognormal baseline is untuned.
